svg.text: A forecasting task goes into a sandbox; what comes out is checked by computation and by a narrow judge
A forecaster's job, stated as a product:
an outlook, a calibration, a verification.
The sandbox: no network, fixed budget
Delivers a fixed envelope, any method:
a private reference under every defensible reading of the brief,
so a known wrong reading is named as a pitfall;
rules every valid answer obeys; skill against withheld observations
the agent's own code on changed data: the results must follow
the data, and must not use what a valid method may not use,
such as a held-out year or a forecast from the future
Claude Opus 5.5, one narrow question at a time, on exact
quotations only: does the report say what the code and the
numbers say, and state its uncertainty in plain language?
No human per run. A scientist certifies each task's reference and pitfalls once.
Each cell: pass rate, cost, time. Change one thing at a time.
The agent keeps its earlier work.
Compare with a fresh run: does work
accumulate, and what does it save?
Forecast tasks also take an optimised
Under what conditions can a forecaster's task be handed to an agent system and come back right? Per task, per system and per tooling, with the same checks each time.
